features.t: Service scaling, ingress and CPU allocation (request-based / instance-based billing)
x: Billing is not metered; the console mirrors the cpuIdle setting but Vyomi does not charge for instance time.

features.t: Source (inline function entry point, runtime, code)
x: "Save and redeploy" is enforced, not just stored: a source/runtime/entry-point edit changes the revision's image fingerprint, so the same revision-diff logic the Admin API uses for any template change cuts a real new revision (visible on the Revisions tab, traffic following it) exactly as a redeploy would.

features.t: YAML view of the service config
x: The YAML view is generated read-only from the real service state; editing and re-applying YAML directly is not simulated — use the other tabs.

features.t: Continuously deploy from a repository (Cloud Build / GitHub)
x: Build from GitHub (core/ci_core.py): connecting a https://github.com owner/repo (optionally with the user's own personal access token, stored server-side) and choosing Build from GitHub fetches the branch, builds its Dockerfile with BuildKit on the offline appliance and cuts a revision whose image is the really built one; no Dockerfile (no buildpacks), no outbound HTTP or container builder (Nano), or a failed build ends FAILURE with the reason and leaves the service untouched. The built image stays in the host docker engine (not pushed to Artifact Registry); Cloud Source Repositories, GitHub App/OAuth authorization and webhook-triggered builds are not simulated.

features.t: Event triggers (Eventarc) and Cloud Build source deploys
x: Vyomi only has a real event source for Pub/Sub-sourced ("Custom event") triggers: creating one validates the topic exists and creates a real Pub/Sub subscription; each published message really invokes the destination service once (no invoker check, as the trigger's service account is implicitly granted run.invoker).

features.t: Observability (request metrics, container instance count, logs)
x: Metrics (request count, request latency, container instance count) and Logs are fed by real activity — the console's own invoke calls and real Eventarc trigger deliveries — never random/synthetic data; a service nobody has called shows zeros.
Worker pool instance splits across revisions are not modelled; a worker pool always runs its current template.

features.t: Domain mappings (map a custom domain to a service, DNS records)
x: Vyomi does not provision a real TLS certificate or serve traffic on the mapped domain; the DNS records it returns are illustrative.
GPU-backed functions run on NVIDIA L4 hardware; Vyomi has no GPU passthrough or scheduler.

features.t: Networking (HTTP/2 end-to-end, session affinity, VPC egress, service mesh, custom audiences)
x: These are validated configuration on the revision/service, enforced and round-tripped like the real Cloud Run Admin API v2: ports[].name http1/h2c (one port, ingress container only), sessionAffinity, vpcAccess (connector in the same region that must exist in the VPC core, or one Direct VPC interface whose subnetwork must exist, egress ALL_TRAFFIC / PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY, network tags), serviceMesh resource name, and customAudiences.
